statement: A zero-dimensional osculating Grassmannian Schubert problem has its Schubert intersection number of distinct real solutions at distinct real osculation parameters, and the intersection is transverse.

answer.text: For a zero-dimensional osculating Grassmannian Schubert problem, the generic complex count is its Schubert intersection number, equivalently the specified tensor-product singular-weight-space dimension. Corollary 6.3 realizes exactly this many distinct real points at distinct real osculation parameters and proves transversality.

source.location: Corollary 6.3(ii), PDF p.28; Theorem 6.1 and Corollary 6.2, pp.26–27

notes:
The row retains arbitrary conjugation-invariant osculation data. Distinct real parameters supply a transverse witness and hence the generic complex count; no claim that every nonreal-parameter fibre is reduced is made. The weight λ includes the specified condition at infinity in the source notation.

The 2007 paper explicitly distinguishes the earlier Mukhin–Tarasov–Varchenko proof of reality from its new transversality theorem. The earlier reality result is recorded here as background; the intersection-number/representation-dimension equality itself is classical.

For a zero-dimensional osculating Grassmannian Schubert problem, the generic complex count is its Schubert intersection number, equivalently the specified tensor-product singular-weight-space dimension. Corollary 6.3 realizes exactly this many distinct real points at distinct real osculation parameters and proves transversality.

The following bibliography supplies historical attribution or supporting background for the result. Evgeny Mukhin, Vitaly Tarasov, Alexander Varchenko, The B. and M. Shapiro conjecture in real algebraic geometry and the Bethe ansatz (2009, mukhin_2005_shapiro).
scope: Zero-dimensional Grassmannian Schubert problems restricted to flags osculating one rational normal curve; real lower bounds allow conjugate pairs, total reality/transversality requires distinct real osculation points.
